messages:
elaine (pm): Quick sync — Sales surfaced a firm request from an enterprise customer: they want an SLA with 99.95% uptime + p99 token latency <150ms for `chat-compact` on hosted API. Need PRD acceptance criteria, graceful-degradation plan, and what we can reasonably commit to. Who can weigh in?

maya (eng-ml): Clarify scope: is the SLA for hosted only? Dedicated/private have different guarantees. Also p99 150ms depends a lot on model variant and quantization.

priyanka (sales-eng): Customer is fintech, global (US/EU). They'll sign if we provide cross-region SLA, rollback policy, and clear credit terms. They pushed hard on p99 150ms for their primary route.

devon (infra): 99.95% availability is feasible with multi-AZ + warm failover. Latency p99 <150ms is tough when batching and autoscale warmup are involved. Need per-model perf numbers and per-region routing.

sam (sre): Proposal: separate SLO (internal objective) vs SLA (contract). Suggested defaults: SLO Availability 99.95% for paid tier, 99.9% for free. Latency SLO: p95 <80ms, p99 <200ms baseline; make p99 150ms an optional target for tuned models. Also define error budget math.

elaine (pm): Draft acceptance criteria (for PRD) — please comment inline:
```
- SLA: 99.95% monthly uptime measured per-route at edge gateway for paid customers
- Latency: p95 < 80ms; p99 < 150ms for `chat-compact` in region us-west1 under production traffic mix
- Error budget: <= 0.05% failed requests monthly (HTTP 5xx + timeouts)
- Graceful degradation: automatic fallback to `chat-small` with `X-Redwood-Fallback: true` header and client-visible warning; circuit-breaker to stop retries after 3 consecutive failures
- Rollout: 10% canary for 48h, automated rollback if error budget burn >50% during canary
- Observability: per-route latency shards, token-level billing logs, and 1s-resolution p99 tracking
```

maya (eng-ml): Add: automated rollback if error budget exceeded for 3 consecutive days or if region p99 spikes >2x baseline. Also require a canary test harness (synthetic load + prompt set).

devon (infra): Need infra knobs in PRD: circuit-breaker thresholds, max-inflight per-instance, batch-size upper/lower bounds, autoscale warmup seconds, and k8s HPA config. Also include cost delta table for lower-batching (more instances => higher cost).

priyanka (sales-eng): Sales asks we include credit policy formula in PRD: credit = min(10% monthly invoice, (SLA_target - observed_uptime)/SLA_target * monthly_invoice). They want this explicit.

sam (sre): Test plan acceptance items: regional failover DR test, synthetic 95/99 latency soak for 72h, canary 10% traffic for 48h with chaos injection (simulate instance loss). Also include runbook links.

ops-bot: Deploy plan created: infra/prod/slo-rollout-176120, canary window 48h, owners: devon, maya, sam.

elaine (pm): Action items: Maya — finalize PRD SLO section by EOD Fri; Devon — attach infra config snippets and cost delta; Sam — create test checklist and runbook stubs; Priyanka — summarize negotiation levers for contractual language. We'll reconvene Monday to sign off.

priyanka (sales-eng): I'll push back on global p99 in the SLA unless we can guarantee region-specific commitments. That's usually acceptable to customers.

maya (eng-ml): Quick Q: should PRD include explicit performance/cost tradeoff table (batch size vs latency vs tokens/sec)? I think yes.

devon (infra): Yes — include a small table with example deltas and recommended defaults (batch=4, max-inflight=120, warmup=60s).

sam (sre): I'll start an "operational playbook" doc for graceful degradation + credit calculation + incident thresholds.

elaine (pm): Great. I'll post the PRD draft link here when it's ready: https://redwood-internal/drive/prd-slo-sla-176120. Thanks everyone.
